title: Today the tresses will be combed
takeaway: Real love asks a lot of you. People who truly love keep going anyway.
scene: Picture a street in a Punjabi village. Word has gone around that the most beautiful girl in town is going to comb out her long hair today. The young men who are in love with her are already waiting outside. The poet tells it as if a battle is about to start.

original: اَج زُلف سنواری جانی اے، کئی دِل تڑفائے جانے نیں
کئی الّھڑ ہیرے بے دوسے وچ خاک رُلائے جانے نیں
transliteration: Ajj zulf sanvaari jaani ae, kayi dil tarfaaye jaane nain
Kayi alhar heeray be-dosay vich khaak rulaaye jaane nain
translation: Today she will comb her hair, and many hearts will ache for it.
Many innocent, precious young hearts will be thrown in the dust, though they did nothing wrong.
couplets.story: Today she is going to comb her hair, and the poet warns that a lot of hearts are about to get hurt. Young, innocent people who did nothing wrong will end up crushed, just from seeing her.

original: کئی دید دے طالب دیوانے تیری راہواں دے وچ بیٹھے نیں
اَج سِدھے ترچھے نیناں دے کئی تیر چلائے جانے نیں
transliteration: Kayi deed de taalib deewaane teriyaan raahvaan de vich baithe nain
Ajj siddhe trachhe nainaan de kayi teer chalaaye jaane nain
translation: Lovers desperate for one look at you are sitting along your path.
Today your glances, some direct and some sidelong, will strike them like arrows.
couplets.story: Lots of lovesick people are sitting along her road, hoping for one look. But her look is dangerous. Whether she looks right at them or glances sideways, it hits them like an arrow.

original: واپُرے دی آ کے چھیڑ گئی کنج زُلف لہراندی اے ویکھو
اَج عاشق زار دیوانیاں نوں ایہہ ناگ لڑائے جانے نیں
transliteration: Vaa purey di aa ke chhed gayi, kinj zulf lehraandi ae vekho
Ajj aashiq-e-zaar deewaaniyaan nu eh naag laraaye jaane nain
translation: The east wind brushed past and set her hair rippling. Look at it move.
Those dark curls are like snakes, and today they will be turned loose on the heartbroken lovers.
couplets.story: Then a breeze blows in from the east and lifts her hair. It moves like a snake. The poet says those curls really are snakes, and today they will be set loose on lovers who are already falling apart.

original: اے دل تُوں ہمت ہاری نہ اجے اوہدیاں ریجھاں لتھیاں نئیں
اِک وار نئیں کئی وار اَجے ایہہ تیر چلائے جانے نیں
transliteration: Ae dil, toon himmat haari na, ajje ohdiyaan reejhaan lathiyaan nahin
Ik vaar nahin, kayi vaar ajje eh teer chalaaye jaane nain
translation: Heart, don't lose your nerve. She hasn't had her fill yet.
These arrows won't come once. They'll come again and again.
couplets.story: Now the poet talks to his own heart. Don't give up, he tells it. She isn't finished yet. You won't get hurt just once. You'll get hurt again and again.

original: تاہیوں پیا زخم چھپاناواں میں اپنے یار جراحاں توں
تُوں تھاں تھاں بھنڈیا جاویں گا جد پھٹ وکھائے جانے نیں
transliteration: Taahiyon piya zakhm chhupaanaa vaan main apne yaar jarraahaan ton
Toon thaan thaan bhandiya jaaven ga jad phatt vikhaaye jaane nain
translation: So I hide my wound, even from the friends who could heal it.
If I showed it, your name would be gossiped about everywhere.
couplets.story: He has been hiding his pain, even from friends who could help him. Why? If people saw how hurt he was, they would ask who did it, and her name would be gossiped about all over town. He would rather suffer than let that happen to her.

original: ہُن آ جاؤ سارے سودائی جنہاں سر دا سودا کرنا ایں
دربارِ حُسن وچ اج سارے جانباز بُلائے جانے نیں
transliteration: Hun aa jaao saare saudaai, jinhaan sir da sauda karna ain
Darbaar-e-husn vich ajj saare jaanbaaz bulaaye jaane nain
translation: Come now, all you lovesick ones, ready to trade your own head.
Beauty is holding court today, and everyone willing to risk their life is called.
couplets.story: Then he calls out to everyone who is crazy enough to risk everything for love. Come on, he says. Beauty is holding court today, and only the brave are invited.

original: ایہہ مُڈھوں عشق دی ریت رہی تا حشر وی رہنی اے احمدؔ
کجھ پُٹھی کھل لہا رہے نیں کُجھ دار چڑھائے جانے نیں
transliteration: Eh muddhon ishq di reet rahi, taa hashr vi rehni ae Ahmad
Kujh putthi khall lahaa rahe nain, kujh daar charhaaye jaane nain
translation: Ahmad, this has been love's way from the very beginning, and it will be until the end of time.
Some lovers are flayed alive, and others are led up to the gallows.
couplets.story: In the last lines the poet says his own name, Ahmad. That is how this kind of poem always ends. Now he stops joking. This is how love has always worked, he says, and it will stay this way until the end of the world. Real love costs something. Some lovers were skinned alive. Some were hanged. He is thinking of famous Sufi saints who were killed for the love they would not give up.

deeper:
In Sufi poetry, the person the poet loves is often a way of talking about God. Read that way, this poem says something bigger.

The girl combing her hair is God showing His beauty to the world. The people waiting in the street are seekers who long to feel close to Him. The arrows and snakes are the pain of that longing: once you have caught a glimpse of God, ordinary life can't fill you anymore. Hiding the wound is the seeker keeping their love quiet and humble instead of showing it off.

The last couplet says it straight. The great lovers of God, like Mansur and Shams Tabriz, gave everything, even their lives. The poet says that has always been the price of real devotion, and always will be.
why: This is the poem the book is named after. It starts out playful, with hair like snakes and looks like arrows. Then it ends with something serious: love that is real usually costs you something, and the people we remember most are the ones who were willing to pay.
prompt: What do you care about enough to keep going, even when it's hard?
notes: Couplet 3: I read the opening word as 'vaa purey', the east wind. If a native reader sees a different word, only the first half of the line changes.
Couplet 7: 'lahaa rahe nain' is read as 'are having (their skin) pulled off'. The flaying image is clear either way.
